Q0407

“In pursuing learning, one increases day by day; in pursuing the Way,…” — Laozi (Daodejing, Ch. 48)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Daodejing, Ch. 48. Theme: way.

Quotes / Laozi / Q0407

English

In pursuing learning, one increases day by day; in pursuing the Way, one decreases day by day. Decreasing and decreasing again, one arrives at non-action.
Thinker Laozi
School Daoism
Source Daodejing, Ch. 48
Theme Way
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Daodejing, Ch. 48 and files it under Daoism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Laozi

Laozi is the traditional sage-author of the Daodejing, though historical identity and textual formation remain contested. Early tradition places him in the sixth century BCE as an older contemporary of Confucius; many scholars see the received text as composite and later.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Laozi and Confucius), way is framed through Confucianism and Daoism. Some passages define way; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through way, action.

Concepts in this quote

Way
Way appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat way as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Action
Action concerns agency: what it is to do something intentionally, and how thought becomes practice.
